items.followUp: Describe the roles of the small intestine in digestion.

rubric.why: The stomach mechanically mixes food with gastric juice.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that muscular contractions churn or mix food.

rubric.why: The answer should identify stomach secretions and explain their roles in digestion.
rubric.description: Gastric juice: hydrochloric acid and pepsin
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for hydrochloric acid providing an acidic medium (or killing germs) and 1 mark for pepsin digesting proteins into smaller peptides.

rubric.why: Mucus protects the stomach from its acidic contents, and the partly digested food leaves the stomach as chyme.
rubric.description: Protection and onward passage of food
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the protective role of mucus and 1 mark for describing chyme passing into the small intestine.

modelAnswer: The muscular walls of the stomach churn and mix food with gastric juice.
Hydrochloric acid in gastric juice makes the contents acidic and helps kill germs.
Pepsin digests proteins into smaller peptides.
Mucus protects the lining of the stomach from acid and digestive enzymes.
The partly digested, semi-liquid food is called chyme and passes into the small intestine.

rubric.why: Horticulture provides useful plant products for people.
rubric.description: Provides food and useful plant products
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid benefit such as producing fruits, vegetables or flowers.

rubric.why: A second distinct benefit may be economic or environmental/aesthetic.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a different valid benefit, such as income, employment or beautification.

modelAnswer: Horticulture provides fruits, vegetables and other useful plant products for people.
It provides income and employment, and the cultivation of ornamental plants beautifies the surroundings.

items.followUp: What is biotechnology, and how is it useful to people?

rubric.why: Bioeconomics links biological knowledge or resources with economic use.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that it concerns the economic use of biological knowledge, resources or products.

rubric.why: The answer should state how this knowledge is useful.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it helps use biological resources efficiently or gain economic benefits from them.

modelAnswer: Bioeconomics deals with the economic use of biological knowledge, resources and products.
It helps people make effective use of biological resources and gain economic benefits from them.

items.followUp: In an experiment, what is the purpose of keeping a control group?

rubric.why: The control group does not receive the factor being tested and is kept under normal conditions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly describing the control group.

rubric.why: The experimental group receives the factor whose effect is being investigated.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly describing the experimental group.

modelAnswer: The controlled group is kept under normal conditions and does not receive the factor being tested.
The experimental group receives the factor being tested so that its effect can be observed.

items.followUp: Differentiate between qualitative and quantitative observations.

rubric.why: Quantitative observations are measured or expressed numerically.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying quantitative observations as the more accurate type.

rubric.why: Measurements and numerical results are less dependent on personal judgement.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that quantitative observations are measurable, numerical or more objective.

modelAnswer: Quantitative observations are more accurate than qualitative observations.
They are measured and expressed in numbers, so they are less dependent on personal judgement.

items.followUp: List the main steps of the biological method.

rubric.why: A biological problem is the question or issue that needs to be investigated.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining a biological problem as a question or issue about living organisms.

rubric.why: The biological method is the systematic procedure used to investigate and solve such a problem.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the biological method as the steps or procedure used to solve a biological problem.

modelAnswer: A biological problem is a question or issue about living organisms that needs to be investigated.
The biological method is the systematic procedure used to investigate and solve a biological problem.

items.followUp: Name the cell organelle discovered by Christian de Duve and state one function of it.

rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that he received the Nobel Prize in 1974.
